scenario: [RDSC.11.1] No padding is admitted: an artefact ends at the end of its last atom, every byte after an atom begins a frame, and a trailing 0xFF is a malformed frame, refused with DS_ERR_DSC_DECODE (-503). The loader must not stop at such a byte and load the atoms before it: an erased tail is a truncated rule bundle ([RDSC.9.7]). The program compiles to 40 atoms, so `runtime_error`'s `tamper: {insert_bytes: {at: 40, hex: "ffff"}}` ([RCTS.1.2.21]) appends two 0xFF octets after the last atom, as erased flash after an image would. A count other than 40 makes the tamper no site (fewer atoms) or puts the octets before the last atom (more). The walk reaches the DscHeader first, so `dsc_sha256` is re-sealed over the edited artefact and the refusal is the padding's, not the hash's. Twin of RDSC.11.1_trailing_zero_padding_is_decode. What it discriminates: a loader that stops at an erased byte loads the 40 atoms; one that reads 0xFF as the start of a varint still arriving answers TRUNCATED, -500. PATHS: libds's `ds_dsc_load` atom walk (`ds_pbf_next_atom`: the byte is not 0x0A, MALFORMED before any varint is read); the Mercury runtime's `ds.atom.next_frame` (`ae_bad_outer_tag`) in `ds.dsc`'s walk, through test_behave.m's `bytes_inserted` and `libds_load_status`.
rules_ds:
use default

schema NoKey scope logical:
    entity_id: String mutable
    v: Int mutable

schema Out scope ttl 1_h:
    tag: String

rule touch:
    NoKey
->
    emit Out tag: "seen"
